title: Architecture 21 conference
transcript:
Speaker 0: Have some time to look at questions one through five. Now we begin. You should answer the questions as you listen as the recording is not played twice. Listen carefully to the conversation and answer questions one to five.
Speaker 1: School of Architecture, Professor Bert's office.
Speaker 2: Oh, good morning. I was wondering if you could give me some information about the forthcoming Architecture twenty one conference dates, enrollment procedures, costs, that sort of thing?
Speaker 1: Uh-huh. Well, the conference runs from the eighteenth to the October 20.
Speaker 2: Eighteenth to the October 20. Oh, good. I'll still be here then. And, where exactly is it being held? Is it at the university as in previous years?
Speaker 1: No. It's actually being held at the Pacific Hotel. We've rather outgrown the university conference facilities, so we've opted for this new venue.
Speaker 2: Right. Paradise Hotel.
Speaker 1: No. The Pacific. That's p a c I f I c.
Speaker 2: Oh, right. And presumably, we can get accommodation at the hotel?
Speaker 1: Yes. But you'll need to contact them direct to arrange that. I'll give you the number for hotel reservations. Have you got a pen ready?
Speaker 2: Yes. Go ahead.
Speaker 1: It's area code 07 93332266.
Speaker 2: And what's the registration fee?
Speaker 1: Individual fees are $300 for the three days or a $120 a day if you only want to attend for one day.
Speaker 2: Are there any student concessions?
Speaker 1: There's a 50% concession for students, so that's a $150 for the three days or $60 a day.
Speaker 2: And am I too late to offer to give a talk?
Speaker 1: Oh, I'm pretty sure you've missed the deadline for that.
Speaker 2: Oh, really? But I've only just arrived here in Australia. Is there any way I could have a paper accepted?
Speaker 1: Well, you'd need to talk to professor Bert, the conference organizer. I can put you through if you like.
Speaker 2: That'd be great. Oh, and can I just check the spelling of his name? Is that b u r t?
Speaker 1: Yes. That's correct.
Speaker 0: You have some time to look at questions six to 10. Now listen carefully and answer questions six to 10.
Speaker 3: Professor Bert speaking.
Speaker 2: Oh, hello. My name's John Helston. I'm an architecture student at London University. I'm here in Australia for three months looking at energy saving house designs.
Speaker 3: Right.
Speaker 2: I'm interested in giving a talk on my research at the conference, but I believe I may have missed the deadline.
Speaker 3: Well, strictly speaking, you have. The closing date was last Friday.
Speaker 2: Oh, no.
Speaker 3: But we may be able to include your paper if it fits into our program, but you'll have to be quick. Okay.
Speaker 2: What do I need to do?
Speaker 3: Send me a summary of your talk, and make sure you include an interesting title for the talk, something to attract people's attention.
Speaker 2: Okay. Interesting title. Right. I'm looking at ways of designing buildings for tropical climates that don't rely on the need to include air conditioning. So I'm sure I can come up with something.
Speaker 3: Yes. Quite. But remember, the outline should be no more than 300 words.
Speaker 2: Right. I'll try to keep it down to 300 words, but would 400 be okay?
Speaker 3: No. Not really because we have to print it in the proceedings, and we just don't have the space.
Speaker 2: Sure. I understand.
Speaker 3: And also, can you send me a short CV? The usual stuff, name, age, qualifications, that sort of thing.
Speaker 2: Right. Okay. Short CV.
Speaker 3: Actually, you can email it to me. That'd be quicker.
Speaker 2: Sure. What's your email address?
Speaker 3: Well, the best thing would be to send it to the conferenceadministrativeofficer@info, that's info,@uniconf.edu.au.
Speaker 2: Right. I'll do that straight away.
Speaker 0: That is the end of section one. You will now have half a minute to check your answers.
